validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: overwhelmingly confirmed, real, correctly classified as an interstate transmission trunk. Independent origins found: (1) FERC/Federal Register dockets CP05-357/358/359/360 (initial 7(c) certificate application filed by Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline Company, May 23 2005 notice, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2005/06/08/E5-2920/) and the May 2006 FEIS availability notice (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2006/05/11/E6-7199/) -- both government-published dockets, independent of the operator; (2) Cheniere's current operator page (https://www.cheniere.com/about/where-we-work/creole-trail-pipeline) states: 94-mile, 42-inch, bidirectional pipeline, ~1.5 Bcf/d, in service spring 2008, connecting Sabine Pass LNG to Transco/TETCO/Trunkline/NGPL interconnects; (3) PHMSA operator registry independently lists 'CHENIERE CREOLE TRAIL PIPELINE, L.P.' as a registered pipeline operator (https://primis.phmsa.dot.gov/enforcement-data/operator/32264); (4) Industrial Info Resources, Oct 19 2007 (independent trade press, contemporaneous), describes construction starting on the 137-mile-scope Creole Trail pipeline's Phase I (80 mi of 42-in pipe) from Sabine Pass LNG NE through Cameron/Calcasieu/Beauregard/Allen/Jefferson Davis/Acadia parishes -- names contractors Willbros-RPI (design) and Sunland Construction (spread 1); (5) Natural Gas Intel, Apr 28 2015, reports FERC clearing the Creole Trail Expansion Project [CP12-351] for service, quoting FERC's gas-engineering director directly, confirming the Gillis Compressor Station (Beauregard Parish) reversal project; (6) a 2013 Cheniere/Cheniere Partners PR Newswire release confirms 'The Creole Trail Pipeline is a 94-mile pipeline' and documents Cheniere Partners' purchase of it; (7) Law Insider's public-contract database independently republishes a legal-agreement definition of 'Creole Trail Pipeline' as 'approximately 94 miles of 42-inch diameter natural gas pipeline ... FERC Docket Nos. CP05-357-000, CP12-351-000, and CP13-533-000' -- ties the original certificate and both later expansion dockets to the SAME pipeline, confirming no duplicate/relabel candidate exists on the roster (no other PID names Creole Trail or its expansion). ROUTE/ENDPOINTS: sheet's StartLocation=Beauregard Parish / EndLocation=Sabine Pass LNG is consistent with Cheniere's own routing description (Sabine Pass LNG -> Johnson Bayou -> NE to interconnects near Gillis Compressor Station, which NGI's 2015 article places in Beauregard Parish); the line is explicitly bidirectional so Start/End labeling is a geographic, not flow-direction, convention -- not a concern. StartYear1=2008 matches all sources. Capacity=1500 MMcf/d (1.5 Bcf/d) matches Cheniere's current figure and is close to NGI's 'up to 1.53 Bcf/d' post-2015 reverse-flow figure. CITATION POOL: opened all 8 harvested wiki citations. cheniere.com/pipelines/creole-trail/ and cheniere.com/where-we-work/creole-trail (both original wiki cites) are confirmed dead (HTTP 404) -- replaced with the live current Cheniere page at /about/where-we-work/creole-trail-pipeline (same publisher, current content, verified). naturalgasintel.com Sabine Pass Trains 5/6 article and the 2006 Federal Register FEIS notice are both live and used. Argus Media (2017, Transco receiving gas from Sabine Pass LNG) is live (200, names the pipeline) and corroborates ongoing bidirectional operation post-2015 but was not needed for any specific cell. IJGlobal's citation is a paywalled search-results page (not fetched -- inaccessible, not evaluated). eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is the generic Pipeline Projects navigation page flagged tracker-wide as not citable for a specific value (per batch guidance) -- not cited. nola.com's Sabine Pass LNG storage-tank-leak article does not name Creole Trail Pipeline (verifier: name_found=false) -- correctly excluded, it is about the LNG terminal, not this pipeline.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1 from 'Cheniere Energy' to 'Cheniere Energy Partners' (ticker CQP) -- a distinct, separately-traded public entity from Cheniere Energy Inc (ticker LNG). Verify with entity_lookup.py before staging to avoid creating a duplicate owner entity if 'Cheniere Energy Partners' already exists on the operators/owners tab.
validity.researcher_notes: Cheniere's own current page states the owner explicitly: 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P., owns the Creole Trail Pipeline' (https://www.cheniere.com/about/where-we-work/creole-trail-pipeline). 'Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P.' (NYSE MKT: CQP) is a separate publicly traded master limited partnership from 'Cheniere Energy, Inc.' (AMEX/NYSE MKT: LNG), the parent/general-partner-affiliate -- they are not interchangeable entities, though related. This is independently corroborated by a May 29, 2013 joint Cheniere Energy Partners/Cheniere Energy Inc. press release on PR Newswire documenting the actual transaction: 'Cheniere Partners purchases Creole Trail Pipeline as previously contemplated ... In connection with the Creole Trail Pipeline purchase, a subsidiary of Cheniere Partners has entered into a $400 million senior secured term loan facility' (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cheniere-partners-completes-financing-and-commences-construction-on-sabine-pass-liquefaction-trains-3-and-4-purchases-creole-trail-pipeline-209316521.html). This confirms ownership passed TO Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. in 2013 and has remained there through the current Cheniere.com page (2 independent, dated sources agreeing the current owner is Cheniere Energy Partners, not Cheniere Energy Inc). The sheet's current Owner1='Cheniere Energy' 100% appears to name the wrong entity in the Cheniere corporate family.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat SegmentCost=$800,000,000 as confirmed. Verify against a Cheniere/Cheniere Partners 10-K capitalized-cost disclosure or the original FERC certificate order's cost estimate before relying on it; none of the primary-source figures found independently support $800M as stated.
validity.researcher_notes: Three different cost figures surfaced across primary/contemporaneous sources, none of which is $800,000,000: (1) Industrial Info Resources, Oct 19 2007 (independent trade press, contemporaneous with construction): 'the design and engineering contract for the $200 million-plus pipeline project was awarded to Willbros-RPI' -- describes the original Phase I (2007-2008) construction scope. (2) The May 29, 2013 Cheniere/Cheniere Partners PR Newswire release: 'a subsidiary of Cheniere Partners has entered into a $400 million senior secured term loan facility' in connection with Cheniere Partners' 2013 PURCHASE of the already-built pipeline plus funding the reverse-flow modification capex -- an acquisition + expansion financing figure, not an original construction cost. Neither figure, nor their sum (~$600M), cleanly matches the sheet's $800M. I could not locate a primary source (FERC certificate cost estimate or a Cheniere/Cheniere Partners 10-K capitalized-cost line item naming this specific pipeline) that states $800,000,000 for Creole Trail. This is flagged as a material spec disagreement per the corroboration standard (a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not just mention the pipeline) -- not asserting a specific correct replacement value, since none of the three found figures cleanly represents a single all-in total-project cost either.

fills.researcher_notes: The 2005 Federal Register notice (a government publication of FERC's docket record) states the exact filing date (May 23, 2005) for Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline Company's 7(c) certificate application in Docket CP05-357-000; the SEC-filed Cheniere/BusinessWire release from later that same year independently corroborates the project was actively before FERC in 2005. NOTE: the pipeline as originally proposed (116.8 mi dual 42-in + 46.9 mi single 42-in + a 6.8-mi lateral to a since-abandoned Dominion Gas Storage facility, serving BOTH Sabine Pass LNG and a second, never-built 'Creole Trail LNG' import terminal) was substantially larger than what was ultimately built (94 mi, serving only Sabine Pass LNG) -- the Creole Trail LNG terminal project was separately abandoned (see 2007 Federal Register 'Notice of Application for Amendment ... and Application for Abandonment', E7-15522) and the pipeline scope was scaled back accordingly before the 2008 in-service date. This does not change ProposalYear (the 2005 application date stands regardless of later scope reduction) but is worth another researcher's awareness if the Creole Trail LNG terminal's own GEM entry (separate from this pipeline) is ever reviewed.

Searched Cheniere's operator page, the FERC Federal Register notices opened for this row, PHMSA's operator page, and general web search for 'Creole Trail Pipeline MAOP psig' / 'maximum allowable operating pressure' -- no source states an MAOP or operating-pressure figure for this line. The original FERC certificate order (Docket CP05-357, not directly opened -- only the FEIS-availability and application notices were reachable via Federal Register/govinfo without a slower eLibrary session) likely states a design/MAOP figure but was not retrieved within this pass. Left blank rather than inferring a typical 42-inch interstate MAOP.

Per gem_schema.md's FuelSource gotcha, this field wants a named upstream field/plant, not the commodity type. Creole Trail Pipeline does not have a single named upstream source: it was built (2008) to deliver regasified, foreign-sourced LNG imported at Sabine Pass LNG into the interstate grid (Transco/TETCO/Trunkline/NGPL); after the 2015 CP12-351 reversal and the CP13-552/553 Zone 1/2 expansion it instead gathers domestic feed gas FROM those same interstate/intrastate systems (plus Pine Prairie Energy Center storage, per the NGI 2015 Trains 5/6 article) TO Sabine Pass LNG for liquefaction/export. Neither direction maps to one discrete field/plant the way a gathering-line FuelSource would. Left blank rather than defaulting to 'Natural Gas' or naming an arbitrary interconnect.

summary: P0283 Creole Trail Pipeline: existence/classification strongly confirmed (7 independent sources incl. FERC dockets, PHMSA, Cheniere, IIR, NGI, PR Newswire, Law Insider); staged refs for Status/Fuel/Start/Capacity/Length/Location/Operator plus fills for Diameter=42in, ProposalYear=2005-05, ConstructionYear=2007-09, and a bonus StartYear2=2015-04 (reverse-flow expansion in-service). Two concerns filed: Owner1 likely wrong ('Cheniere Energy' should be 'Cheniere Energy Partners', per Cheniere's own site + the 2013 PRNewswire sale) and SegmentCost=$800M unsupported by any primary source found ($200M 2007 construction estimate and $400M 2013 acquisition/expansion loan found instead).
